ideas: What you were saving for and why
How it felt when you reached your goal

phrases.meaning: keep money to buy something later
keep money for a special purpose

model: I'd like to talk about the time I saved up for a trip to Japan, which was about two years ago. I'd wanted to go there since I was a student, but flights and hotels are expensive, so I realised I'd need around forty million dong. At the time, I wasn't saving anything at all, which meant that I had to change my habits quite a lot. The first thing I did was to keep track of every single thing I spent for a month. That was a bit shocking, to be honest, because I found I was spending nearly a third of my salary on food and coffee. So I decided to cut back on eating out and started cooking dinner at home and bringing lunch to work. I also cancelled two subscriptions I hardly used. Every payday, I would set aside a fixed amount in a separate savings account, so I couldn't spend it by accident. It wasn't always easy. My friends kept inviting me to expensive restaurants, and saying no led to some awkward moments. But I tightened my belt for about ten months, and as a consequence, I had enough money for a ten-day trip in cherry blossom season. The whole experience gave me a real sense of achievement. I didn't feel guilty at all when I treated myself to a nice dinner in Kyoto. It also taught me that small changes result in big savings over time.
